item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
item.description: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

item.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
item.description: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.

item.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says
item.description: The East Coast's weather is a major concern this holiday, as it could lead to coastal flooding. And, the judge says the FCC can't punish ABC for satire Trump doesn't like.

item.title: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia
item.description: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

item.title: Africa Cup title given back to Senegal after sports court rules against Morocco
item.description: Senegal won the Africa Cup on the field in Morocco in January and then lost it in a legal case in March because its players walked off the field in protest in second-half stoppage time.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
item.description: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama has vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned. But an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.
item.content:encoded:
